page: Microsoft Azure NC8as_T4_v3 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine from the NCASv3_T4 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system incorporates an x86_64 AMD processor configured with 8 dedicated virtual CPUs and 56 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 7.0 GB RAM per vCPU core. Local storage is provided via an integrated 378 GB solid-state drive (SSD), and the instance architecture is compatible with Premium Storage. It operates without complimentary public IPv4 addresses, requiring standard virtual network configuration for external connectivity.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by a single NVIDIA T4 GPU equipped with 16 GB of video memory. The configuration maintains a high memory-to-vCPU ratio alongside GPU capabilities, facilitating tasks that require both host-level data staging and accelerator execution. The included 378 GB local SSD acts as temporary scratch storage suitable for intermediate data caches, model weights, or input pipeline buffers, reducing reliance on remote disk operations during execution phases.

From a resource allocation perspective, the pairing of an entry-level datacenter GPU with moderate core density and 56 GB host RAM provides an economical entry point into GPU-accelerated compute compared to large multi-GPU infrastructure. The primary architectural tradeoff is the single-GPU limit and the reliance on the T4 architecture rather than newer generation matrix engines. NC8as_T4_v3 is suited for machine learning inference, GPU-based rendering, video transcoding, lightweight model fine-tuning, and compute workloads requiring dedicated hardware acceleration.
description: Microsoft Azure NC8as_T4_v3 is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine belonging to the NCASv3_T4 family, provisioned on Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is powered by an AMD x86_64 processor delivering 8 dedicated virtual CPUs paired with 56 GB of system RAM, yielding a resource ratio of 7.0 GB of memory per core. Compute operations are augmented by a dedicated NVIDIA T4 graphics processing unit featuring 16 GB of VRAM. For temporary data and high-speed scratch space, the instance includes 378 GB of local SSD storage and supports Premium Storage configurations. The hardware combination of dedicated AMD compute cores, substantial host memory capacity, and targeted hardware acceleration provides an entry-level GPU architecture. This makes the instance cost-efficient for specialized tasks without the overhead of massive multi-GPU configurations. The instance is suited for machine learning inference, graphics processing, video transcoding, visual computing, and general-purpose workloads requiring hardware-accelerated processing.
